items.title: A card's accent rim can change colour but not weight
items.evidence: Every rung draws its rim as `border: 1px solid var(--glass-border-accent)` (src/styles/glass/ladder.css:72 wash, :96 quiet, :112 resting, :140 floating, :159 overlay). The accent mixes colour only (src/styles/glass/rim.css:69-73, `--glass-accent` at `--glass-accent-strength`). No width token exists: `git grep` in src for `--glass-accent-width`, `--glass-border-width` or `--glass-rim-width` finds nothing. The only `border-width: 2px` on a card is the `cartoon-surface` utility (src/components/card/styles.css:258), which widens the box. Card already tweens box-shadow and border-color on one clock (card/styles.css:85-87). The selectable card's focus ring owns the outline (card/styles.css:155-158), so the heavier leg has to be an inset box-shadow. Where it is composed matters. `--glass-material-rim` is declared on `:root` (rim.css:53-55), so a leg written into it resolves once there, and a card's own `--glass-accent-width` or `--glass-accent` would never reach it. That is why `--glass-border-accent` is composed per element, on the rung selectors (rim.css:56-73). `--card-cast` is declared on `.card` (card/styles.css:76-80), so it composes per element too. The leg has to stay in the list at every width, with zero spread at the 1 px default: a shadow list that gains an inset entry partway through stops interpolating, and the change would switch in one frame instead of tweening. release/11.1.1 adds only a reduced-motion press fill to card/styles.css (+198-213 there); rim.css and ladder.css are untouched. No booked row covers it: INBOUND O-381 is the scrim and CommandDialog, and O-337 is the focus ring.
items.row: G3 (O-413). Adds one token, `--glass-accent-width`, default 1px (today's look). It is drawn as an inset leg inside the rung's edge, so the box never changes. The leg is composed at the element, in the rung group beside `--glass-border-accent` (rim.css:56-73) and in `--card-cast` on the card, never in the `:root` `--glass-material-rim`. It is present at every width (zero spread at 1 px), so it tweens on the box-shadow clock the card already uses for border-color. A new token makes it a minor, and it belongs with neither the dock nor the Metric pass, so 11.3.0. HELD: not built until atlas confirms after the owner's first preview. Witness, as atlas states it: a card with the accent at 2 px has the same box as the card at rest, to the pixel, in both themes. Glass reads it in both engines, and the default stays 1 px.
items.reply: Glass can add a weight for the accent rim in 11.3.0: up to 2 px, drawn inside the card's edge so its box never changes, and tweening with the colour. We'll hold it until you tell us the owner's first look needs it, and today's 1 px rim stays the default.

items.title: No hover surface that can be anchored to a point of data
items.evidence: Part (1) is already shipped. PopoverContent takes `reference`: an element, or a virtual `{ getBoundingClientRect }` (`PopoverVirtualElement`, src/components/popover/PopoverContent.vue:19-49). It is passed to reka at :90-91, and reka's HoverCardContentImpl and PopperContent both accept `reference` (node_modules/reka-ui 2.10.1, HoverCard/HoverCardContentImpl.js props), so it works on the hover arm as well as the click arm. Without a trigger, reka's grace area is simply not installed (shared/useGraceArea.js: its watchEffect needs both elements). Open it through `v-model:open` on Popover with no trigger (Popover.vue:15, :50, :76-79). Landed in 7e22fd6f4 (2026-11-09); `git tag --contains` gives v11.1.0 only, and v10.1.2 and v11.0.2 have no `reference`. Booked as INBOUND O-82 and O-178. Part (2): the open and close delays have been props since before atlas's version (v10.1.2 Popover.vue:21-23, :59-60; master Popover.vue:20-23, defaults 250 and 150 at :59-60), so atlas can set 0 and 120 on what it ships today. Part (6), the gap from the reference, is `sideOffset` today (default 4, PopoverContent.vue:66-72; collision padding 16 at :93). Not present: (a) a new reference re-places the content in one jump (the comment at PopoverContent.vue:44-46; `git grep popper-content-wrapper -- src` is empty, so nothing glides); (b) the content takes the pointer from its first frame, and nothing sets `data-entered` (no match in src on master or release/11.1.1); (c) nothing keeps the card clear of the pointer. Part (5): on release/11.1.1 the popover and hover card enter and leave on opacity and a short slide (release/11.1.1 CHANGELOG.md:34-42). PopoverContent there emits `leave-finished` (release/11.1.1 PopoverContent.vue:162-167, attrs at :190). The study's later 'one opening for every popup' (INBOUND O-410, O-414 G6) would change that entrance for every popup, hover cards included. Coarse pointers drop the hover arm (Popover.vue:81-85). A new component is ruled out by docs/precepts/restraint.md:109 ('One variant per job').
items.row: G11 (O-413). Not a new component: restraint.md:109 allows one variant per job. The work is additive options on Popover and PopoverContent: (a) a glide on the glass spring when `reference` changes while open; (b) the content passes the pointer through until the reader enters it, marked `data-entered`; (c) a clearance that keeps the content off the pointer's position. New props make it a minor outside the dock and Metric passes, so 11.3.0. The default delays stay 250 and 150 ms, since changing them would change a default; atlas sets 0 and 120 itself, which it can do on 10.1.2 already. Already met: (1) since 11.1.0; (2) as props since before 10.1.2; (6)'s 16 px gap from the reference through `sideOffset`; (5) as 11.1.1's popover entrance, which follows any later change to the shared popup opening (O-410, O-414 G6). Witness, as atlas states it, in both engines.
items.reply: Since 11.1.0 a Popover can already open on a virtual rectangle with no trigger (`PopoverContent :reference` with `v-model:open` on `Popover`). Its open and close delays are props you can set to 0 and 120 today, and `sideOffset` gives the 16 px gap from the rectangle. In 11.3.0 glass adds the rest as options on that same Popover rather than a new component: a glide on glass's spring when the reference moves, the pointer passing through until the reader enters the card (marked `data-entered`), and a gap that keeps the card clear of the pointer.

items.title: A collapsible dock in the flow changes its own box and slides its persistent buttons
items.dedupe_of: O-366a (dock redesign RU-61, amended by RU-84; joins 11.2.0 only on the owner's question 14). The morph-state ask duplicates the redesign's LEDGER L-53, atlas's earlier ask 2.
items.evidence: On master an in-flow collapsible dock grows its own box when it opens. Glass's hover-shift sweep measured this: INBOUND O-366a, 104 to 445 px, held until the 6 s fold. `anchor` only writes `data-anchor` (src/components/dock/README.md:60-62; GlassDock.vue:432). Booked: RULINGS-6 RU-61 (docs/tranches/BL/design/dock/wi8/RULINGS-6.md:119-132) has the open plate lie over its row and grow away from the anchored edge. RULINGS-7 RU-84 (RULINGS-7.md:266-274) found that the prototype's open plate covers 1,872 px² of atlas's legend and its link while the dock lingers. So RU-61 joins 11.2.0 only on the owner's answer to question 14 (RULINGS-7.md:518; default: no change in 11.2.0), and the atlas draft says to keep the layout hold (RULINGS-7.md:538). An explicit `anchor` outranks a persistent seat (RULINGS-6.md:130): atlas's PlateDock sets `anchor="end"` with Table in `#persistent`, so even with RU-61 Table slides the full growth unless it moves to `#persistent-end` or the dock takes `anchor="start"`. The linger is the owner's order (INBOUND O-275); the fold waits `DOCK_COLLAPSE_DELAY_MS` = 6000 (src/components/dock/constants.ts:60). Morph state: `data-morphing` is set on the `.glass-dock` root when the morph arms (src/components/dock/composables/useDockMorph.ts:84) and removed at settle (:67). The root is at GlassDock.vue:423-425, passed in at :235. It is present at v10.1.2 (useDockMorph.ts:76 at that tag). On bl/dock/wi8 (db66eeb0e) it is set on any posture or content change (useDockBody.ts:877-885) and removed at rest (:1254), which is what LEDGER L-53 asked (docs/tranches/BL/design/dock/wi8/LEDGER.md:107, atlas ask 2). The README does not name it. It is already public surface: docs/tranches/BL/audit/dock-usage/SURFACE.md counts the root's data attributes as items (:31, :154) and lists `data-morphing` as used by value.js, gregg, atlas and daraksha (:156). RULINGS-7's name budget counts root attributes too: it removes `data-dock-scope` and `data-dock-glyph` as names. So naming it in the README adds no name and the 78 stands. The seat's claim of 78 to 79 does not hold.
items.row: G12 (O-413) duplicates O-366a, which feeds W-I.8 RU-61 as amended by RU-84. It joins 11.2.0 only if the owner answers question 14 (grow away from the legend, keep a reserve, or no change in 11.2.0, the default). Atlas's q6 measurement is a further witness for RU-61's gate on atlas's head-row cell. The morph-state half is LEDGER L-53, met on bl/dock/wi8, which sets `data-morphing` on posture and content episodes. The 11.2.0 README names it as the public morph signal. That adds no name, since root attributes are already counted, and needs no new event. The atlas draft also carries the anchor note: `#persistent-end` or `anchor="start"`.
items.reply: Keeping an in-flow dock's box still is in the 11.2.0 dock redesign, but it waits on the owner's call, because the open plate would cover part of your figure's legend and its link while the dock lingers. Until he answers, an in-flow dock still pushes its row, so please keep your own reservation. Even after it lands, Table stays put only if it moves to `#persistent-end` or the dock takes `anchor="start"`. The morph state you asked for is already there. Since 10.1.2 the dock's root has carried `data-morphing` from the start of each morph until it settles. In 11.2.0 it is also set while the dock's content changes size, and the README names it.

items.title: Menu and select rows have no place for a leading mark, and mark the selected row with a dot
items.evidence: SelectItem draws its selected mark as a dot in the start gutter (src/components/select/SelectItem.vue:76-84). The gutter is rowClass's `start` arm (src/components/_shared/menu/rowClass.ts:27-30), and `hideIndicator` removes both mark and gutter (SelectItem.vue:55-58). Its slots are the default and `description` only (:86-91). No rule paints a selected select or menu row at rest. The `aria-selected="true"` rules in src CSS are the contrast and forced-colours arms (src/styles/accessibility.css:13, :34), the dock trigger's specular (src/styles/glass/material.css:371) and the dock layer tab (src/components/dock/styles/layer-group.css:294), and none reaches a `.glass-menu-row`. DropdownMenuRadioItem draws `menu__radio-dot` in a leading `menu__indicator` (src/components/menu/DropdownMenuRadioItem.vue:46-50, styled at src/styles/glass/overlay-plate.css:262-268) and declares a default slot only (:25). SegmentedTabs has had a scoped `#option` slot since v10.0.0 (src/components/tabs/SegmentedTabs.vue:271-273). It replaces the label, and selection is the sliding plate (:218-234), not a dot. Its narrow form, a Select, prints `opt.label` only (:173-181). The `#option` slot does not reach it, and it cannot be routed into a SelectItem `mark` because it carries the label as well, which would print twice. Booked and related: INBOUND O-393 (11.1.2, docs/tranches/BL/driver/glass-11.1.1-scope.md:136-138) already names DropdownMenuRadioItem. In a group with leading icons its indicator moves to the trailing slot and the leading column holds icons only; a group with no icons keeps it leading. It adds no slot and no non-dot indicator. Also related: O-414 G17 (value.js's menu layouts: one aligned icon column, tick trailing). release/11.1.1 touches none of the three components (only a press fill in src/components/_shared/menu/menu.css and the bar radius in tabs/styles/segmented.css).
items.row: G14 (O-413). Adds a named leading `mark` slot on SelectItem and DropdownMenuRadioItem, sized and aligned by glass. SegmentedTabs gets a scoped `#mark` (`option`, `active`) as well: drawn before the label in the strip, and passed to SelectItem's `mark` in the narrow form. `#option` cannot do that job, since it replaces the label. New slots are new API outside the dock and Metric passes, so 11.3.0. When `mark` is filled, the mark takes the leading column O-393 sets up in 11.1.2, and the selected state is a trailing check, the form O-393 ruled and value.js's study (O-414 G17) repeats. Since that form is already ruled, no new owner question. `aria-selected` and `aria-checked` are unchanged. Rows without a mark keep today's dot. Related to O-393 and O-414 G17, not a duplicate of either. Witness, as atlas states it: in both themes and right to left.
items.reply: In 11.3.0 SelectItem, DropdownMenuRadioItem and SegmentedTabs get a leading `mark` slot that glass sizes and aligns. A row with a mark shows it is selected with a check at the row's end, not a second dot. In SegmentedTabs's strip `#option` already takes your dot today, and its selection is the sliding plate. The new slot is what carries the dot into its narrow form, a Select, which prints only the label today.

items.title: Glass has no component for a drawn icon
items.evidence: src/components at master holds no icon, glyph or mark component (directory listing). Pieces already exist. The dock seat's glyph share is `--dock-icon-glyph-ratio`: 0.5 on master (src/styles/tokens/sizing.css:179) and 0.9 on bl/dock/wi8 (sizing.css:179). There the seat sizes its direct `svg`, `img` or `picture` to that share (bl/dock/wi8 src/components/dock/styles/controls/icon-button.css:249; RULINGS-5 RU-45; RULINGS-7 RU-76, RU-87). So a part that renders a bare `<svg>` as a seat's child is already sized by the dock's rule, and a second 10/11 constant inside the part would be a second authority for one share. RU-45 took 0.9 from the owner's own 40 px in 44 (docs/tranches/BL/design/dock/wi8/RULINGS-5.md:80-81). His strip at 0.5, 0.75 and 0.9 is still owed before 11.2.0 takes it (OWNER-READ.md:101, question 9). Ten elevenths of a 44 px place is 40 px, 0.9 is 39.6 px. The selected ring hook is `--dock-active-shadow` (sizing.css:255, read at src/components/dock/styles/controls/icon-button.css:203, and kept on bl/dock/wi8 at :195). daraksha builds the same thing on these tokens at origin/master 3a26717: src/shell/PageIcon.vue draws `<svg><use href>` sized from `--dock-control-size` times `--site-glyph-fill` (:19-20, :25-31) and is `aria-hidden`, with the name on its seat (:19). Lift and press are in src/shell/SiteDock.vue:376-391, the 1.5 px ring at :397-398. Two sites want it (atlas, daraksha), and as an exported part it meets the overfitting law. No booked row covers it. O-409 (less padding round dock glyphs), RULINGS-7's glyph rulings and value.js's study questions 1 and 3 (glyph size, drawn against line icons) cover size and drawing manner only. Home Assistant's LF-35 is the dialog close glyph.
items.row: G15 (O-413). A new part: a drawn icon that takes a symbol address or id. It draws flat fills through `<use>`. It takes an accessible name when it stands alone and is `aria-hidden` when its place already carries a name (a DockControl's label), so it is not announced twice. Its size is the place's glyph share, read from the dock's one token (`--dock-icon-glyph-ratio`) rather than a second 10/11 constant. A host that wants ten elevenths exactly sets that token, and the owner's size strip (dock question 9) picks the default. The drawing alone lifts 2 px and scales to 1.08 on hover and gives to 0.92 on press, on the compositor. It fades under reduced motion and paints CanvasText under forced colours. The selected ring comes through `--dock-active-shadow`. A new part is a minor. 11.2.0's ready list is closed and the redesign is cutting names, so it goes to 11.3.0. The owner's 'like daraksha' sets the look, using daraksha's values. Witness, as atlas states it.
items.reply: Glass will ship a drawn-icon part in 11.3.0 modelled on daraksha's. It draws a symbol through `<use>` with flat fills that inherit your colours, and takes an accessible name when nothing beside it names it. It fills the same share of its place as the dock gives its glyphs (set that share to ten elevenths if you want exactly 40 px in 44). The drawing alone lifts on hover and gives on press, it fades under reduced motion, and it paints CanvasText under forced colours. Until then, 11.2.0's dock is set to size an icon that is a seat's direct `svg` to nine tenths of the seat, pending the owner's look at the sizes, and `--dock-active-shadow` already draws the selected ring.

changed: G3: the mechanism note was loose. The leg must be composed at the element (rim.css:56-73, `--card-cast` at card/styles.css:76-80), not in the `:root` `--glass-material-rim` (rim.css:53-55), where a card's own width could never reach it. It must also stay in the shadow list at every width so the change tweens. The witness now quotes atlas exactly (both themes) and adds the engine read as glass's own. Verdict and release kept.

G11: added that the delays have been props since before atlas's 10.1.2 and that `sideOffset` already gives atlas's 16 px gap from the reference (PopoverContent.vue:66-72), so the reply now says so. Part (5) is tied to the later shared popup opening (O-410, O-414 G6). Verdict and release kept.

G12: 'naming data-morphing adds one name (78 to 79)' is wrong. SURFACE.md:31, :154-156 already counts root attributes and lists data-morphing as used by four apps, atlas included, and RULINGS-7's budget counts attributes as names, so the 78 stands. The morph-state ask also duplicates LEDGER L-53 (atlas's ask 2), met on bl/dock/wi8 (useDockBody.ts:877-885). Corrected line cites: question 14 is at RULINGS-7.md:518, the anchor clause at RULINGS-6.md:130, the README at :60-62. Verdict and release kept.

G14: the reply's 'SegmentedTabs needs nothing new' does not hold. `#option` replaces the label (SegmentedTabs.vue:271-273), so the narrow Select form (:173-181) cannot route it into SelectItem's `mark` without printing the label twice, and SegmentedTabs needs its own `#mark`, as atlas asked. O-393's 11.1.2 text already names DropdownMenuRadioItem (scope :138). The 'only aria-selected rules' claim was overstated: material.css:371 and layer-group.css:294 also match, though neither reaches a menu row. O-414 G17 added as related. Verdict and release kept.

G15: a 10/11 default inside the part would be a second authority for the share. The seat rule already sizes a direct svg to `--dock-icon-glyph-ratio` (wi8 icon-button.css:249), and the owner's size strip (question 9) is still owed, so the part reads the one token. The part also needs to be aria-hidden inside an already-named place, as daraksha's is (PageIcon.vue:19). The reply hedges 11.2.0's 0.9 as pending the owner's look. The overfitting-law wording was corrected. Verdict and release kept.
